title: Excused Credit Hours on a Reduction - Education Benefits Training Notes
content:
**Training notes for Veterans Service Representatives — excused credits under Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education).**

The student's excused credits are the dropped credits VA treats as dropped on the last date of attendance rather than from the term start. Which dropped credits are excused depends on how VA treated the reduction and on whether it is the first reduction ever reported on the benefit.

**Rule.**
1. When VA accepted mitigating circumstances for the reduction on the student's evidence, every credit dropped is excused.
2. When VA did not accept mitigating circumstances on evidence and the reduction is the first ever reported on the benefit, the credits dropped are excused up to the tier's one-time exclusion of the first 6 credit hours a student ever drops.
3. When VA did not accept mitigating circumstances on evidence and an earlier reduction is on the benefit, the one-time exclusion has been used and no credit is excused.

"An earlier reduction" means any other reduction in credits reported on the benefit besides the one being measured.

**Questions answered from the rule**

*Mitigating circumstances accepted on evidence, 9 credits dropped — how many are excused?* All 9 (point 1); the 6-hour figure plays no part.

*No evidence accepted, first reduction on the benefit, 4 credits dropped?* 4 — below 6, every dropped credit is within the exclusion (point 2).

*No evidence accepted, first reduction, exactly 6 credits dropped?* 6 (point 2).

*No evidence accepted, first reduction, 8 credits dropped?* 6; the 2 credits above the exclusion are not excused (point 2).

*No evidence accepted, a reduction already reported earlier on the benefit, 3 credits dropped?* None (point 3).

| Mitigating circumstances accepted on evidence | First reduction ever reported on the benefit | Credits excused |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes or No | Every credit dropped |
| No | Yes | Credits dropped, at most 6 |
| No | No | None |
